title: Naturally present metal ions in plants could interfere with common antioxidant assays
author: Tomova, Petkov, et al.
materials: Single electron delocalization of phenoxide radical in those of polyphenols with ortho or para hydroxyl groups makes this reaction thermodynamically favorable and the free radical formed may further react with a second radical; a reaction that turns the phenolic group into a stable quinone structure. Both the configuration and the total number of hydroxyl groups substantially influence the antioxidant activity of polyphenols.

steps.title: Extract plant material with methanol
steps.instruction: Weigh 5 g of each plant material (Ginkgo biloba kernels, Tamus communis rhizomes, Asplenium ceterach leaves). Add 50 mL of 70 % methanol, stir at room temperature for 8 h in a light‑protected place. Filter through Whatman No. 1 filter paper, then repeat the extraction two more times with fresh 70 % methanol. Combine all filtrates and store the combined extracts at 4 °C until analysis.

steps.title: Determine dry matter of extracts
steps.instruction: Take two parallel aliquots of each combined extract, evaporate to dryness, and weigh the residue to obtain dry‑matter content gravimetrically. Record the average of the two measurements.

steps.title: Prepare Chelex® resin
steps.instruction: Place commercial Chelex® resin in a container, add enough 70 % methanol to cover, and stir overnight. After stirring, remove the methanol and air‑dry the resin.

steps.title: Chelate extracts with Chelex resin
steps.instruction: Weigh 5 g of the conditioned Chelex® resin and add 25 mL of a plant extract (from step 1). Stir the mixture overnight at room temperature.

steps.title: Test for residual redox‑active metals
steps.instruction: Apply the ascorbic acid autoxidation test (as described in reference [11]) to the chelated extract to confirm the absence of free or loosely bound redox‑active metal ions.

steps.title: Filter chelated extract and determine dry matter
steps.instruction: Filter the resin‑treated extract to remove the resin, collect the filtrate, and determine its dry‑matter content gravimetrically in duplicate.
